answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: starting from trusted seeds, the endpoint distribution assigns weight to each vertex. A sybil cluster, whether tagged juniper or basalt, must cross a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits escape probability, while conductance and min-cut bounds cap its reachable trust mass and thus its aggregate voting weight, regardless of how many colluding identities it creates.
